scope: Proposition 8.5 (The secular quadratic terms) of the manuscript “BKT universality for height and planar spin fields” (preprints/BKT-universality-for-height-and-planar-spin-fields-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5e6a8df09e021c4a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 129. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: In the continuum limit at a′ = k0, the balanced coefficients are independent of the scale and satisfy btt = 0, btz = −b < 0, bzz = −H < 0. (8.20) The positive numbers b, H stay in compact subintervals of (0, ∞) as u ranges over the compact interval in Lemma 8.1. Consequently, given ε > 0, one can first take µ0 small and then ρ large so that, uniformly in j, |btt j | ≤ ε and −btz j , −bzz j lie in fixed compact positive intervals. For every fixed J the same conclusion follows by making the starting scale sufficiently large. At that fixed J the coefficients converge to their continuum limits as j → ∞ when a′ = k0. For the fixed-J entry family, use its own multipliers λen j and its own projection operators in the same balanced coordinates. Its critical continuum coefficients are btt en = 0, btz en = −ben, bzz en = −Hen, ben = 2 log L, Hen = 8π · π 4 e8πcυen log L > 0, υen = v √ 32 . At this fixed J, the corresponding discrete coefficients converge to these limits at criticality and have the stated positive bounds on a sufficiently small one-sided reference interval once m is large. If d is the largest power of two not exceeding the sup range of J, then uwh = v/(d √ 32) is the width of the first fixed-J family at the same block ratio, and Hen = d4Hwh, whereas ben = bwh. These entry-family bounds are not uniform in a varying J.
